llm_synthesis.name: Carnot-Guided RNA Thermodynamic Efficiency
llm_synthesis.description: The blend treats guide RNA spacer targeting as a reversible information engine that converts chemical free‑energy gradients into sequence‑specific binding work. By mapping the cyclic isothermal‑adiabatic steps of a Carnot engine onto the hybridisation‑dehybridisation cycle of CRISPR complexes, a universal efficiency bound for target recognition emerges, analogous to the Carnot limit. The paradigm predicts that maximal targeting specificity is achieved when the free‑energy drop across the binding cycle equals the thermodynamic limit set by the cellular temperature gradient.
llm_synthesis.emergentProperty: A Carnot‑type upper bound on CRISPR targeting efficiency that couples information entropy reduction (target discrimination) to thermodynamic free‑energy consumption, defining a maximal specificity‑per‑energy ratio unattainable by any guide RNA design.
llm_synthesis.isomorphismMapping: Guide RNA complementarity ↔ Isothermal heat exchange; Binding free‑energy ΔG ↔ Work output W; Off‑target dissociation ↔ Adiabatic expansion; Temperature of cellular environment (T_cell) ↔ Hot reservoir Th; Effective mismatch temperature (T_mismatch) ↔ Cold reservoir Tc; Efficiency η = (specificity gain)/(ΔG) ↔ Carnot efficiency η_C = 1 - Tc/Th; Reversibility of binding cycle ↔ Reversible Carnot cycle.
llm_synthesis.falsifiableTest: Design a library of guide RNAs spanning a wide ΔG spectrum and measure (i) on‑target cleavage rate, (ii) off‑target binding frequency, and (iii) cellular temperature. Compute empirical efficiency η_emp = (ΔInformation_gain)/(ΔG). Verify whether η_emp ≤ 1 - (T_mismatch/T_cell) holds across all designs; systematic violation would falsify the Carnot‑guided efficiency bound.
